subject: ela
intro: Ninth graders analyze how complex characters (those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme. A complex character is not simply good or bad; their mixed motives drive the story.

steps: A complex character has multiple or conflicting motivations.
So they are not simply good or bad; they have mixed, competing motives.
solution.answer: They have multiple or conflicting motivations, not simply good or bad.

items.prompt:
Read.

Torn between loyalty to his friend and his duty to the law, the officer hesitated, then made the arrest.

How does this conflict make him complex and advance the plot?

steps: He has two competing motives (loyalty vs duty).
His struggle and choice drive the action.
So his conflicting motives make him complex and his choice advances the plot.
solution.answer: His competing loyalty and duty make him complex, and his choice drives the plot.

items.prompt: How can a complex character develop the THEME?

steps: Their struggle embodies the text's central idea.
So their conflict can dramatize the theme (e.g., duty versus loyalty).
solution.answer: Their inner conflict can dramatize the text's theme.

items.prompt: A character with conflicting motives is ____.
A character who changes over the text ____.
A character's choices can ____ the plot.
